shots.fix: Use the light cyan title color from the palette instead of white. Make the y-axis labels and bar labels slightly larger for easier reading.

Titles should be light cyan (accent) rather than white. Show a clearer y-axis break, or add value labels, so the truncated 98.2 baseline is obvious. Otherwise the chart matches the phrase: the truncated axis exaggerates a small change, so 'This year' looks towering next to 'Last year'.

Change the callout text to match the spoken line, e.g. 'Do what most people skip' with 'skip' as the emphasis. 'First, the axis' introduces a different topic from 'It's a little scary, right?'. For on_style, shift the callout off-centre or top-left and add a brace or label.

Keep the left label from clipping off the canvas edge: shift the number line right or shrink or reposition the 'y-axis bottom: 98.2' label. Add a title or caption beneath the line to fill the empty space.

Add a brace or label between the bars reading '+0.2' to show the actual change. Show the full 0-100 axis or a faded comparison so the small difference reads clearly. Make the title cyan and centered per the palette, and change 'Crime Is Skyrocketing!' to a neutral title such as 'Real values'.

Keep the callout; it shows a tiny +0.2 change, which answers the rhetorical question well. To match the style better, move the equation off-centre or top-left, and add a label or brace such as 'tiny change' beside the +0.2. The title should be centred at the top in light cyan, not a small left-aligned tag.

The phrase says the bars didn't move at all, but the chart shows a truncated axis (98.2 to 98.6) that makes 98.3 vs 98.5 look like a big jump. Set y_min to 0 and y_max to 100 so the bars look nearly identical, and drop the axis-break marker. Alternatively, keep the truncated chart and set both values equal (e.g. 98.3 and 98.3). Also make the value labels brighter for contrast.

Text is centred and the layout is sparse, so it fits the black canvas, but the style notes call for an off-centre or top-left visual with attached labels. Move the callout off-centre and add a small axis sketch beside it. The cyan emphasis on 'axis begins' already matches the spoken point.

Style: the title 'Crime is skyrocketing' is white rather than light cyan, and the chart fills the canvas instead of sitting off-centre with generous empty space. Change the title to 'Honest axis from 0' or similar so it matches the 'redraw honestly' phrase and the misleading headline isn't repeated, and color the title in the cyan accent.

Title slightly overlaps the top of the bars and value labels; move the title higher or add padding. Use light cyan for the title to match the palette, and use the cyan accent for the non-highlighted bar.

Add labels tying 0.2 to 'difference' and 98.3 to 'base' (e.g. braces). Move the equation off-centre or top-left per the layout. Drop the dark gradient for pure black, and use a centred cyan title if one is needed.

Move the title lower or add space so it doesn't crowd the 98.3%/98.5% value labels, and make it light cyan to match the palette. The y-axis could start at 0 and keep the bars looking like physical objects, e.g. with a 3D or block-stack look, but a prop-only fix is to set the title to 'Imagine the bar as a physical object' and keep highlight_index 1.

Titles are centred in yellow and cyan rather than light cyan, and the 'WORKED EXAMPLE' tag and divider add clutter. Make both titles light cyan, and make the y-axis tick labels and the truncated-axis break marker larger and brighter.

Optionally add a brace or label on the bars (e.g. a '3x' callout) so the 'three times' claim is explicit. Otherwise the truncated y-axis, with its break marks, already shows how a small change was made to look three times larger.

Show the verdict caption 'Bottom 98.2 is hidden' beneath the charts to fill the empty lower third. Brighten the grey value labels on the right chart (98.3%, 98.5%) so they match the white labels on the left.

Style is only partly matched. Move the chart off-centre or to the top-left with a caption or formula beside it, as the layout describes. The bars could also use accent2 yellow for emphasis. The centred title is fine.

Move the equation off-centre or top-left as the layout describes, and add a brace or label such as 'leftovers' and 'real quantities' to tie the equation to the phrase. The background is a dark vignette rather than pure black, so set it to #000000. Highlight both 3s, or the 0.3 and 0.1, to match the 'leftovers' idea.

Match the phrase: the chart's title and axis should show an alternative cut point such as 98.2, for example 'Cut at 98.2 instead' with y_min 98.2, or add a highlighted marker at 98.2 to show it is arbitrary. Also make the y-axis labels larger and add a left margin so they are easier to read.

Make the truncated-axis effect easier to see: add a small label such as 'axis starts at 98.2' near the yellow break, or enlarge the 98.2 tick label. Move the chart off-centre or top-left with a caption beside it, as the layout notes describe.

Raise the contrast of the '98.3%' label in the right chart, which is grey and overlapped by the break marks. Show the verdict 'Closer cut, bigger gap', which is in the props but missing from the frame. Make the right panel's y-axis labels and title match the left panel's size and brightness. Center the titles in light cyan to fit the style.

The frame catches the morph midway, so the two equations overlap and are hard to read. Hold the final 0.3/0.1 = 3× state longer, or begin the morph earlier so the frame lands on a clean equation. Also move the equation off-centre or top-left to match the layout, and make the highlighted 3× larger.
Titles should be light cyan per the style, but the 'Honest' title is yellow. Consider making both titles cyan and moving the visual off-centre with more empty space.

Add a visual cue for the quick-catch idea, such as a highlighted truncated-axis break or an annotation like 'axis starts at 98.2'. Enlarge the small y-axis labels. Make the 98.2 baseline label more visible.

Orient the number line vertically so it reads as a ruler against the y-axis, and add a y-axis line plus ruler-like tick marks. Move it off-centre per the layout and add a brace or label. Make the labels larger, since the small white numbers are hard to read.

Add a bar or segment extending from zero along the line so 'bar's length means its value' is visible, e.g. a bar of length 50 from zero. Enlarge the labels and move the visual toward the upper left as the layout asks.

Make the title cyan, as the style calls for, and add a highlight or label on the zero baseline, such as a ruler graphic or an arrow marking 0. Move the value labels a little lower so they don't crowd the 100 gridline.
Make the sawed-off chunk more obvious, e.g. a thicker or larger yellow zigzag cut, or a ghosted outline of the removed lower part of each bar. Use the light cyan title color per the palette.

Make the title cyan, as the layout specifies. Add a brace or label on the bars showing the size of the chunk, such as the 0.2 difference. Make the truncated-axis break and the 98.2 label larger so the ruler idea reads clearly.

Place the points proportionally on the number line (axis 0 to 98.3) so the 98.2 cut-edge marker sits right next to the 98.3 bar-top marker. Currently the markers are evenly spaced, which puts 98.2 near the midpoint and contradicts 'nearly all of it'. Offset the two labels vertically so they don't crowd each other.

Show the verdict caption "Nearly all of the bar is cut" (it is missing from the frame), and brighten the small axis tick labels. Make the left bars visibly full-height so the 'sliver' contrast is clearer, and use the cyan title color consistently on both panels.

Make the chart read as an ordinary, unremarkable example. The truncated y-axis starting at 98.2 exaggerates a tiny difference and makes the chart look dramatic. Consider y_min 0 for contrast, or keep the truncation but add a caption. Title the chart in light cyan per the palette, and drop the extra highlight.

Make the title light cyan (#5CD0E6) as the palette specifies instead of white. Enlarge the axis labels and the 'PICTURE IT' tag. Consider labeling the broken axis segment explicitly, for example 'axis starts at 90', so the cut region reads as what was cut.
Move the equation off-centre or to the upper left, and add a bar visual with a brace and label beside it. The frame currently has only centred text and no geometry.
Optionally add a caption like 'Not just a crime chart' to reinforce the 'Not at all' beat. Otherwise no change needed.

Style: the chart is centred and fills the canvas, and the title is white rather than light cyan. Shrink the chart and shift it off-centre or top-left, then set the title colour to the cyan accent. Optionally add a caption or label beside the chart.

Style: the layout asks for the visual off-centre or top-left with braces and labels, but the chart fills the canvas and has no annotations. Shrink it, move it off-centre, and add a label such as '+0.9' or '+0.9%'. Phrase: the narration says 'looks dramatic', and the zoomed y-axis (99.8 to 101) does produce a steep-looking climb. To make the point of the deception clearer, add a caption such as 'looks dramatic' or 'axis zoomed in'.

Optionally enlarge the axis tick labels and the 'THE RULE' tag for legibility. The final point's sharp jump to 100.8 slightly undercuts the 'sideways' message, so smooth it, e.g. set the last point to y=100.

Label the highlighted sliver (e.g. 'last two weeks') and widen the dashed yellow band so the sliver is visible against the ten-year line. Use a darker background and a thin white frame to match the palette and layout.

The phrase 'picture a pie chart rendered in 3D' calls for actual pie visuals, not bar charts. Replace the bars with a flat pie and a 3D tilted pie, or use a single 3D pie scene. Also fix the bar heights: the 50% bars reach only about 47 on the left and 36 on the right, which misrepresents the values. The grey 50% labels on the right are low-contrast, so make them white. Drop the 'Two equal slices' verdict until it is spoken, and use a light-cyan centred title to match the style.

Style: the layout calls for off-centre visuals with generous empty space and light cyan centred titles. Here two full-width charts fill the frame and the panel titles are yellow and cyan. Shrink the split, shift it off-centre, and set titles to light cyan.

Style mismatch: the palette calls for light cyan centred titles and an off-centre visual with braces/labels. Make the left title cyan instead of yellow and consider a lighter-weight layout. The content itself matches the phrase.

Labels 'Cut-off bars' and 'Zoomed line' overflow their circles and are clipped. Enlarge the node radius or shrink the font so the text fits. The edge lines also cross into the center node's text, so anchor them to the circle edges. The layout should sit off-centre with more empty space, per the style notes.

Keep the equation, but move it off-centre or top-left as the layout describes, and use a centred cyan title at the top instead of the small 'THE RULE' tag. Consider adding a label or brace to tie it to the 'size of the number' idea.
Widen the circles or shrink the label font so 'Size ≠ value' and 'Zoomed line' stay inside their nodes. Move the title to the centre top in light cyan to match the style.

Style is mostly fine. The black canvas, white text and cyan highlighted '?' match the palette. The equation is centred rather than off-centre or top-left as the layout describes. The 'THE RULE' label is small, and the screen is otherwise empty, so a brace or label attached to the equation could be added. Optionally shift the equation off-centre and enlarge the header.

Style is only partly matched: the bullet list is centred, while the layout calls for an off-centre or top-left visual with braces and labels. The title should be centred at the top in light cyan, not a small tag at the top left. Consider a larger centred title and a left-aligned list, with the final 'Matches the value?' item highlighted in yellow accent2.
Optionally add a short on-screen caveat label such as 'Truncated axis' next to the yellow break marks. The title 'Crime rate' is white rather than light cyan, so recolor it to match the palette.

Raise the contrast of the struck-through claim, since the gray text is dim against the black. To match the palette and layout, add a small visual, such as a chart or axis sketch, off-centre or top-left. Move the label to a centred cyan title at the top.

Space the values proportionally so the 0°F point sits far from 97, which shows how meaningless 0 is for body temperature. Add a break mark or a 'meaningless' label at 0°F. Move the line off-centre and add some empty space to match the style. Enlarge the small labels.

Make the sick-threshold clearer, e.g. add a y-axis label or a reference line at 98.6 or 100 so the 'single degree' jump reads. The highlight_range could also be tightened to the Thu peak. The title could be cyan and centered per the style, and the chart pushed off-centre with more empty space.

Mostly fine. For style, move the chart off-centre or top-left and add a brace or label (e.g. 'zero baseline') showing the squashed range. Optionally make the title light cyan, and increase the axis label font size.

Move the 'Crime rate' chart titles clear of the bar value labels (the 98.3 and 98.5 labels crowd them on the left chart). Raise the y-axis tick label contrast. Shift the layout toward the off-centre, sparse style with more empty space, and use the light cyan title color consistently (the left title is yellow).

Style: the frame is a split-screen with a top-left label, not the off-centre visual with braces described in the layout. Consider a single chart with a brace or label attached, and put the verdict beside or below it. Content-wise the frame is fine: the same data in both views shows that trend survives zooming.
Move the bullets off-centre or top-left per the layout. Center the title at the top in light cyan instead of the small top-left label. Consider highlighting 'zero' in the accent color for emphasis.

Keep the equation. To match the palette and layout better, move it off-centre or top-left, and consider a centred light-cyan title. The background is a dark gradient rather than pure black, and the 'ONE SUBTLETY' label is top-left instead of a centred title.

Keep the callout, but make it more visual and less bare. Move it off-centre or top-left and add a small ruler or a blob shape with no axis, so it matches the palette/layout notes. Title text could also be centred at the top in light cyan.

Add a dashed line or bracket from the Before bar to the After bar labeled 'half of 2'. Make the title light cyan to match the palette. Consider a lighter bar for After, since it currently reads as a muted teal.

Mostly good. To match the palette/layout, move the equation off-centre or top-left, and add a brace or label such as 'absolute change' under the difference. Also consider a title in centred light cyan, and write the result as '0.01 percentage points' rather than just '0.01%'.

Use 'percentage points' as the unit so it matches the spoken phrase. To fit the layout notes, move the stat off-centre or top-left and put the caption beside or beneath it, with a label or brace attached. Add the thin white frame or a cyan title at the top.

Add the raw counts (2 to 1 in 10,000; 40 to 20 in 100) as sub-labels under each town so the phrase's numbers appear. Make the Town A 0.01 pts label larger or move it further from the baseline. Make the titles light cyan, as the style asks, instead of yellow for 'Relative'.

Make the 'disguise' link clearer: add a visible truncated-axis cue to the right chart, or an arrow from the cut-off bar to the relative % chart. Move the diagram off-centre or top-left per the layout.
Make the small axis labels and the '98.2' break label larger and brighter. To fit the pure-black, sparse style, lighten the background grid and tint the title light cyan.

Optional: the layout notes call for an off-centre visual with a light-cyan title at the top, and this frame is a full two-panel split. Consider a lighter, asymmetric layout and a cyan title instead of yellow for the left heading.

Style: the palette calls for a pure black canvas, but the background here is a dark vignette gradient, and the title is centred in white rather than light cyan at the top. Use a flat #000000 background and move the title to the top in cyan, or add a small visual such as a checkbox icon off-centre.

Frame matches the phrase, with all three questions shown as bullets. Style is only a partial match: the bullet list is centred, while the palette calls for an off-centre or top-left visual. Keep the callout text 'Three questions' with 'Three' emphasized. To match the palette and layout, move the callout off-centre or top-left, and add a small attached label such as a '3' brace. Keep the callout, but add a small visual attached to it (e.g. a brace or label, or a partially revealed number graphic) so it doesn't look like a bare text slide. Place it off-centre or top-left to match the layout described.

Style: the bullet list is centred and plain, while the palette calls for an off-centre or top-left visual with a centred cyan title. Move the list to the left, add a centred cyan title, and consider a yellow accent on 'Next video'.
Let the typewriter animation finish so the full text 'Small exercise' shows. Optionally move the text closer to the top-left and add a cyan accent or small visual to match the style.
